content.title: About
content.content: Cobbler is a small berry crop native to temperate regions of North America. Cobbler berries have a sweet‑tart flavor, an aroma reminiscent of raspberry and blueberry, and a juicy flesh with a slightly crisp skin. They are eaten fresh and also used in baking, jams, juices, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cobbler belongs to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to raspberries and currants.
The berries are rich in anthocyanins, which give them their deep red color.
Cobbler plants can thrive with a short growing season, making them popular among growers in northern latitudes.
Traditionally, indigenous peoples used cobbler berries to make medicinal tinctures.
Cobbler seeds contain a small amount of oil that is used in cosmetic products.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cobbler berries contain vitamin C and polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and flavonoids contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Cobbler berries have a low energy density, making them a good choice for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic responses to cobbler berries, such as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: The berries contain oxalates, so people prone to kidney stones should limit consumption.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Commercially grown berries may be treated with pesticides; it is advisable to wash them thoroughly before eating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cobbler berries can be eaten fresh, added to smoothies, yogurts, and muesli, and are also great in baked goods—pies, muffins, and jams. For sauces, gently mash the berries and mix with a little sugar or honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cobbler berries in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a single layer on a tray, then transfer to a bag—this preserves flavor and nutrients for up to 6 months.
